title: Close the Loop: Taxonomy Feedback
subtitle: Misroutes propose taxonomy changes
scenario: Turn the day's misroutes into taxonomy feedback. Today was clean - zero misroutes - so the honest proposal is: no change needed. Confirming the taxonomy held is as valid a loop outcome as proposing a split. The point is that the taxonomy is maintained, not installed.
input: Archive summary: 3 tickets, 0 misroutes today. No category was reworked, so no category is failing. Feedback: misrouteCount 0, category none, proposedChange none, routed to the Support Ops Analyst for the record.
instructions: Since there were none, set the failing category to none.
Set proposedChange none and route to the taxonomy owner.
Return one valid JSON object, then validate.
copilotPrompt: Build one JSON taxonomy-feedback record: misrouteCount 0, category none, proposedChange none, routedTo Support Ops Analyst. A clean day means no change is needed.
successMessage: Loop closed with 'no change'. A clean day confirms the taxonomy held.
editorHelper: No misroutes means no change - and that is a real result.

sections.title: Maintained, not installed
sections.body: A taxonomy is never finished. Every day's misroutes are a chance to tune it. The loop is how classification stays honest as products and language change.

sections.title: Zero is a signal too
sections.body: Today had no misroutes, so the taxonomy held. 'No change needed' is a real, valuable outcome - it tells Support Ops the categories are working, not that nobody looked.

sections.title: Propose, do not rewrite
sections.body: Even a change proposal routes to the Support Ops Analyst, who owns the taxonomy. The loop informs; the owner ratifies. Feedback never silently edits the category tree.

sections.title: What you produce here
sections.body: A feedback record that closes the temporal loop into the intent taxonomy - confirming it, this time.

fieldGuide.meaning: How many misroutes the day had.
The taxonomy owner, for the record.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd note 'no reclassifications today, taxonomy is fine' so nobody wastes time fixing a category that is working.

tools.powerAutomate: log a 'no change' feedback item to Support Ops
tools.zapier: append a confirmation entry to the change log

takeaway.heading: Loop closed - no change
points: You confirmed the taxonomy held with zero misroutes today.
'No change needed' is a valid, honest loop outcome.
Even proposals route to the Support Ops Analyst - the owner ratifies.
The feedback closes the temporal loop into the intent taxonomy.
The workflow can now maintain the taxonomy from real triage, or confirm it.
